By restricting supervision to informative tokens, this objective ensures that routing gradients are driven by meaningful expert disagreements, allowing the router to capture expert specialization without being dominated by trivial agreement cases. While SFT establishes routing behavior and maintain next-token prediction capability, it does not address how the router should correct expert outputs when the selected expert is locally suboptimal. In practice, experts may produce unreliable logits even when correctly selected. To further improve response quality, we employ an additional preference optimization phase to encourage the router to actively learn complementary logit contribution while treating expert outputs as fixed.
